value.name: Ladder Debris Shaft
value.geometry: 60-ft shaft, 10×10-ft clear interior. Bottom ledge z=0–5 ft, top ledge z=60 ft. Four 15-ft rung segments: S1 z0→15, S2 15→30, S3 30→45, S4 45→60. One fixed wall cable runs z=0→60 with clips at every 5 ft; rated 600 lb total attached load. One creature occupies a rung segment at a time unless actual size/space permits otherwise.

procedures: Clip to safety cable: Action at bottom/top or while adjacent to cable; one free hand. Harness/clip is chamber stock and stays on cable. An attached creature and carried load count against 600-lb capacity.

Climb one 15-ft segment: requires an Action, 30 ft of remaining movement (scene-local 2:1 climb cost), and STR (Athletics) DC14 or DEX (Acrobatics) DC14. The Action and 30 movement are both spent on success or failure. If insufficient movement remains, the attempt cannot begin.

A frightened climber may spend an Action once for that segment to make WIS save DC14. Success grants advantage on its next check for that segment before its next regular turn starts (outside initiative: within 6 seconds); failure grants nothing. This is not the climb Action.

Failure while clipped deals 1d6 bludgeoning and catches at max(0, segmentStartZ−5). Thus S1 failure catches on bottom ledge z=0, never below floor. For S2–S4 the creature hangs 5 ft below segment start.
Recover from a hanging catch above z0: Action plus 10 ft remaining movement to climb 5 ft back to segment-start ledge; no check. This is not a free ascent and does not complete the failed segment.

An ally securely on the destination ledge/segment top may spend Help Action to grant ordinary advantage if physically able; the old +2 is removed to use the current Help interface and avoid stacking a duplicate assistance engine.
value.failure: Three failures by same climber do not end scene; withdrawal downward remains possible. Ordinary actual flight/teleport works if legal.
value.reward: Top ledge holds one finite 50-ft luminous rope (ordinary rope visibility only, no magic bonus).

On successful activation, record traveler identity set, their current body footprints/heights and carried noncreature gear; consume card once. They swap to bounded landing cell for exactly 10:00 elapsed minutes. Noncreature objects lawfully picked up inside a landing cell may return if physically carried at return. A creature not in the recorded traveler set never becomes return-eligible merely by being carried later.

At +10:00 return attempt resolves before same-timestamp local events. Recheck each recorded traveler’s current footprint/height. Place into original marked footprint if legal; otherwise nearest legal chamber placements in stable traveler-ID order. Return of one traveler does not duplicate/remove another. An original traveler being physically carried by another is still placed once as its own traveler identity. Lost/dropped gear stays where actually left.

If any traveler cannot be legally placed, already placed travelers remain returned; unresolved travelers stay in landing cell for a recovery extension of at most 10 minutes with ordinary agency. At +20:00 make second attempt.

If still impossible at +20:00, use emergency pad if current body fits and pad is legal. If pad is physically impossible despite reservation, unresolved travelers enter Return Hold in their landing cell: they are frozen, cannot act/move/interact/harvest or be targeted, and no local clocks/effects newly advance for them. Recheck legal chamber placement every 1 elapsed minute and place them at first legal opportunity in stable ID order. Return Hold grants no continued plane access or onward travel.
Each card remains consumed after successful activation regardless of return delay. No onward portal exists.

Removing a container removes its exact plant identities from this landing cell permanently. Containers have AC10/5HP and ordinary object consequences; destruction/loss never respawns plants. Recognition/harvest may occur later from the same carried container under the flora rules.

A depositing its token immediately meets the all-eligible-resolved close rule, so it cannot then change/deposit another token before a supposed10-minute close. Twelve physical tokens also need a stated procedure when more than twelve independently eligible characters attend; eligibility cannot silently produce a thirteenth token. Leaving/unconscious voters and abstention/token custody need one stable rule.
findings.required: Retain finite one-identity voting. Work deadline/revote with an explicitly unresolved eligible voter keeping the vote open, and a separate single-voter immediate-close case. Define eligibility snapshot/change/overflow and exact token custody without cloning.

value.stock: 12 physical numbered decision tokens, TOKEN-WIND-01..12, 0.05 lb each, fixed chamber stock. At voting-open assign at most one token to each eligible voter in stable Expedition identity order; unused tokens remain in bowl.
value.eligibility: Conscious Expedition character physically present in the entry chamber before voting closes. Temporary summons, pets, companions, minions, projections and scene actors are not voters unless they are independently recorded Expedition characters. A late qualifying Expedition character arriving before closure may receive one unused token; arrival at/after closing timestamp is too late.
value.oneVote: Each assigned identity controls one token. Depositing it in Blue/Amber is an Action. Moving that same token to the other socket before close is another Action and changes the vote. Duplicate/unassigned deposits are rejected and do not count. An eligible voter may declare abstention with brief communication; its token returns to bowl.
value.close: Closes immediately when every then-eligible voter has either a deposited token or recorded abstention, or at exactly +10:00 from scene opening, whichever occurs first. At the exact timeout, close happens before a same-timestamp late arrival/deposit.
value.tie: Count one deposited token per eligible identity. Tie selects Blue by fixed neutral order. One corridor solidifies once; one Wind Token reward at most once.

value.title: Repeated deposit, companion and deadline arrival use one eligibility rule
value.initialState: Voter A assigned token01; pet companion present but not independent Expedition character; Character B arrives exactly +10:00.
steps: A deposits token01 Blue (Action), then tries to deposit another unassigned token: mechanism rejects it. A may only move token01 with another Action before close.
Pet companion is ineligible and receives no token.
At exactly +10:00 timeout closes before same-timestamp arrival/deposit; B is late and gets no token.
Count only legal deposits; if A alone voted Blue, Blue wins.
value.consumedStock: No extra token/reward duplication; one legal deposit.
value.finalState: One vote per identity; companion/late arrival excluded deterministically.

findings.title: Complete Null recipient and lethal-branch ordering
findings.finding: The replacement recipientLifecycle table has no explicit branch for an ordinary nonliving Construct such as Toy Sentinel, although RN-N11 still asserts generic Disabled. Silence Wraith is described as a Spirit significant NPC which disperses, without an explicit relation to that table. The livingCreature text explicitly skips Instant Death/Wounds on positive-to-zero, but already-Dying merely says no added failure; RN-N05 expects no Instant Death/Wounds at Stable0. A qualifying hit that leaves positive HP can still trigger a fatal fourth-Wound save under Core unless the scope is settled.
findings.required: State one ordered Null damage algorithm for positive-to-positive, new zero, existing Dying0, Stable0, source-specific nonliving/created creatures, projections and objects. Decide explicitly where damage-caused Instant Death, Wound/Maiming and existing-fatal-Wound branches are bypassed; preserve independent non-damage expiry/cost events. Bind local actors to actual lifecycle branches, with no anatomy guessed solely from names.

value.scope: At creation of each damage root, record root dealer. If the root dealer is a character currently under unsuppressed Null Veil, mark the entire root `nullNonlethal=true`. Delayed/ongoing descendant packets inherit that flag from the root; later Veil changes do not retroactively change an already-created root. A new later activation/attack creates a new root and re-evaluates.
value.independentCompanions: A companion/minion has its own dealer identity. Controller Veil does not convert companion damage unless an exact ability says the controller is the damage dealer.
value.shared: Pure transfer/redirection keeps the original root's nullNonlethal flag. It does not create a second root or extra prevention/resource triggers.
value.reflection: An effect that explicitly creates new reflected/retaliatory damage uses the reflector as dealer and evaluates that new root at creation. A mere transfer is not reflection.
value.livingCreature: After ordinary mitigation/temp HP, a qualifying packet may reduce a living recipient to 0. If it was positive before the packet and becomes 0, skip damage-caused Instant Death, Wound/Maiming creation, death-save failures and ordinary death; it becomes Stable0 with death successes/failures reset under Core and receives exactly one normal Stable recovery deadline. If it was already Dying0, the packet adds no damage-caused failure but DOES NOT stabilize it, clear counters or change its existing death-save schedule. If already Stable0, it remains Stable and keeps its existing absolute recovery deadline; do not reroll/extend it. If temporary HP absorbs all HP loss and normal HP never reaches0, no zero-state transition occurs.
value.nonlivingCreature: Use recipientLifecycle table; never infer anatomy solely from a name/type label. Objects still use object rule.
value.objects: Objects/noncreature structures take damage normally; 'nonlethal' does not make objects indestructible.
value.preexisting: Does not remove old Wounds/Injuries, revive Dead creatures, clear existing dying counters, rewrite death history, cure conditions, or prevent non-damage lethal costs/tracks. Newly-zero stabilization resets only its current death-save counters because becoming Stable requires that under Core.
value.riders: Independent non-damage riders still resolve if their exact trigger was met and they do not require a Wound/death result.
value.directCosts: Direct HP payments/sacrificial costs are not damage and are not converted.
value.hunt: This nonlethal override does not alter Hunt finality or Hunted Death rules for actual later deaths from other causes.

recipientLifecycle.ordinaryLiving: New positive→0: Stable0 as above. Already Dying0: remains Dying with same counters/deadline markers. Already Stable0: remains Stable with same recovery deadline.
recipientLifecycle.rangerBeast: Source normally dies immediately at0. Qualifying Null damage replaces that damage-caused immediate-death transition with Null Disabled at0: Incapacitated, Speed0, no commands/actions; same animal/bond remains. Ordinary legal companion healing above0 ends Disabled. A later independent non-damage death/removal rule still works.
recipientLifecycle.finiteSummonFamiliarMirrorBeast: Source normally disappears/ends at0. Qualifying Null damage replaces only that damage-caused zero disappearance with Null Disabled at0 while its original duration/source still exists. Independent duration expiry, dismissal, concentration/source end or replacement still ends it. Legal companion healing above0 restores function; no generic repair/resummon is granted.
recipientLifecycle.mageLichElite: Source normally becomes destroyed bound asset at0. Qualifying Null damage leaves same elite Null Disabled at0, not destroyed; therefore Soulbound is not legal solely from this zero. Legal companion healing above0 restores it. An independent actual destruction/expiry can later create its normal destroyed state.
recipientLifecycle.wizardStandardUndead: Qualifying Null damage leaves same minion Null Disabled at0 instead of damage-caused destruction. Dismissal or owner completed-LR expiry still ends it. Legal healing above0 if a real source applies may restore it.
recipientLifecycle.localProjection: A scene projection whose printed 0-HP rule says disperse/end uses that administrative projection endpoint. This is not a living death/corpse transition and is not converted into Stable/Disabled unless that specific actor says so. ACT-FEAST-STEWARD is the explicit exception with Collapsed Projection.
recipientLifecycle.undyingSpellform: If qualifying damage newly reduces a Mage with actual Undying Spellform to0 without killing outright, its printed trigger occurs and its 1/LR use is spent. It overrides zero-HP Unconscious/Incapacitated permissions as reviewed: conscious, half-Speed voluntary movement, normal Action, legal spellcasting/concentration, no independent BA/Reaction. Triggering damage still causes its concentration save. If still0 at feature expiry, the reviewed expiry destabilizes/cancels Stable recovery and adds one failed death save; that later feature-expiry event is not the original Null damage packet.
recipientLifecycle.wouldDieProtections: A protection whose trigger requires actual death/would-die/fatal result does not trigger and spends no use when Null skips that damage-caused death branch. Do not replay it later. Separate minimum-HP prevention that resolves earlier follows its own source if actually triggered.

steps: Resolve packet at0HP.

steps: Root marked nullNonlethal before transfer.
Existing sharing procedure divides packet once.
Each recipient resolves its branch with nullNonlethal flag; no extra root/resource trigger from transfer.
Ordinary defenses follow actual sharing stage.
